name: Midjourney
note: Still the undisputed king of aesthetic quality.
good: Incredible coherence, lighting, and artistic interpretation. V6 is unmatched.
bad: Locked in Discord (though web alpha exists). No API for developers. Hard to get exact composition control.

name: Stable Diffusion (Automatic1111/ComfyUI)
note: The only choice if you need absolute control.
good: ControlNet allows exact posing. Infinite fine-tunes (LoRAs). Free to run.
bad: Steep learning curve. Requires a beefy GPU. Base models often look worse than Midjourney without heavy prompting.

name: Leonardo.ai
note: The best UI for Stable Diffusion workflows.
good: Great built-in models. Real-time generation canvas is magic. Good API.
bad: Generations can sometimes feel overly 'smooth' or plastic. Credit system can be confusing.
price: Free daily credits. Paid tiers start at $12/mo.

name: DALL-E 3 (OpenAI)
note: Best for prompt adherence, worst for style.
good: Actually follows complex prompts with multiple subjects. Spells text correctly.
bad: Heavy censorship. The 'DALL-E look' is very obvious and often overly shiny/cartoony.

name: Krea
good: The real-time canvas where you draw and it generates instantly is the best in class.
bad: Final output quality for complex scenes isn't at Midjourney levels yet.

name: Magnific
good: Adds incredible detail to low-res images. 'Re-imagines' textures beautifully.
bad: Extremely expensive. Can hallucinate weird details (extra fingers in backgrounds) if pushed too hard.

name: Fal.ai
note: The developer API for fast image generation.
good: Incredibly fast inference for SDXL and SD1.5. Great developer experience.
bad: You need to bring your own UI. Not for consumers.

name: Ideogram
note: The best for typography and posters.
good: Spells words perfectly. Great at graphic design styles (logos, posters).
bad: Photorealism isn't as good as Midjourney. Prompting can be finicky.
